divergence: jsonata 2.2.2 answers undefined here. Its processAST gives a bare `%` predicate a parent slot at level 1 where `%.n` gets level 0 (verified in the reference AST: the `a.b[%]` step carries no `ancestor` and no `tuple: true`), so the slot is never filled and `%` evaluates to undefined -- an off-by-one in its static analysis, not a rule. docs.jsonata.org/path-operators defines `%` as 'the enclosing object which has the property representing the context value', which is the `a` object for every context value in `b`, whether the predicate is `%` or `%.n`; that object is truthy, so the filter keeps every item. The same page says an unresolvable parent is a static error S0217, which the reference does not raise either.
